title: When Logic Meets Perception: Operator-Agnostic Differentiable Reasoning for Reliable Neural Prediction

problem.claim: Neural models in high-stakes domains lack access to practitioner-provided ontological constraints.

gap.claim: Existing logical formalisms trade off expressive power against scalability and cannot simultaneously handle the required constraints efficiently.

contributions.claim: A differentiable reasoning framework transforms domain rules into a training objective within a decidable, fully Boolean-expressive logic with guaranteed polynomial-time cost per iteration.
The framework decouples logical structure from continuous semantics and introduces a semantic gate and a structure-aware loss for adaptive training.
The framework injects domain rules into a frozen object detector for semantic image interpretation without extra labels.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The choice of continuous semantics changed performance by over 30 points on the same task.
Across eight benchmark ontologies, the framework achieved statistically significant improvements over nine baselines.
On semantic image interpretation, macro-averaged F1 increased by up to 7.8% without extra labels.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-stakes neural models lack usable ontological constraints because existing logic approaches cannot jointly provide expressivity and scalability.
The paper presents a differentiable reasoning framework with polynomial-time training objectives in a fully Boolean-expressive decidable logic.
The operator-agnostic design exposes large performance variation caused solely by the choice of continuous semantics.
Semantic gating and structure-aware loss adapt gradient focus and objective weighting, removing per-dataset loss tuning.
The framework is reported to improve benchmark ontology results and rule-based refinement of a frozen object detector without extra labels.

source_observation.claim: The choice of continuous semantics alone can substantially affect performance under the same logical task.

interpretation.claim: Semantic operators should be treated as an explicit modeling choice rather than an interchangeable implementation detail.

application.claim: Compare alternative continuous semantics under controlled conditions before selecting one for a constrained prediction system.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported performance sensitivity generalizes beyond the evaluated task.

source_observation.claim: Domain rules improved a frozen detector without additional labels.

interpretation.claim: Structured domain knowledge may improve predictions when labeled data or model retraining is limited.

application.claim: Use validated domain rules as an additional supervision signal for existing models when extra annotation is unavailable.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which rule quality or coverage could limit this benefit.

unknowns: The specific decidable logic and continuous semantics are not identified.
The eight benchmark ontologies, nine baselines, tasks, datasets, and statistical details are not specified.
The abstract does not describe rule quality, constraint coverage, or failure cases.
